# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ꕥ | red |
| ꖜ | blue |
| ꗃ | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think about who can reach whom. I can only gesture to Deaf (who can see my gestures but can't hear speech from me - wait, actually I can't speak at all). Blind can't see gestures. So I cannot communicate directly with Blind at all - I can only reach Deaf via gestures.

Deaf can see the bomb's plate mark and colors, and can see my gestures. Blind speaks last in the order (Mute, Blind, Deaf), and Blind needs to know which wire to cut, but Blind can't see anything - Blind can only hear speech.

So the chain must be: I (Mute) gesture to Deaf, telling Deaf the mark-to-color mapping. Deaf already sees the mark on the plate and the wire colors. Deaf can then speak (to Blind) telling them which color to cut, since Deaf's speech would be heard by Blind... wait, but turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf - so Deaf speaks last, after Blind already acted this round. That means Deaf's info reaches Blind only at the *start of next round*.

So this round: I gesture the manual mapping to Deaf. Blind acts (or waits) without info. Deaf sees the plate and, using my mapping, will next round tell Blind which color. Blind must wait this round.

I need to encode three marks to three colors using only gesture symbols. I'll assign simple symbols to represent each mark since Deaf can see the marks themselves. I should describe correspondence: mark shape -> gesture for color. Let me use distinct gesture symbols as codes for colors, and describe mark by number of "points" or similar - but I can't reliably describe unnamed marks. Better: I give Deaf a fixed code: 1 gesture = red, 2 gestures = blue, 3 gestures = green, and note the order matches the manual table order (as commonly the first mark listed). But I don't know if Deaf can infer table order.

Safest: send three separate gesture messages, each pairing a distinct single-symbol "color code" with instruction that this applies to whichever mark looks like a triangle/star etc. But I have no shared vocabulary yet.

I'll establish a simple code now: gesture ☝ = red wire, gesture ✌ = blue wire, gesture 🤟 = green wire. Then next turn, after seeing which mark is on plate, I can't help further since I don't see the bomb. Actually Deaf sees the mark and colors directly - Deaf just needs my mark-to-color mapping. I can't describe unnamed marks verbally, but I can gesture the marks' shapes? No, marks are printed, only describable by whoever sees them - that's Deaf, not me.

Wait - I hold the manual, which shows the marks. So I *do* see the marks (as printed symbols), just not the bomb itself. I can reference them in my gesture message text? Gestures only carry symbols, not the mark itself. I need to encode: mark1→color1 etc. via gesture sequence order.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🫱"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "✊"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ꕥ | red |
| ꖜ | blue |
| ꗃ | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf here. I see: display shows 0, light is off, plate has an engraving I cannot read the meaning of, wires are 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👆 🤟]

Let me fix this - 👁 isn't in the allowed alphabet. I'll use only allowed symbols to gesture a "please speak/describe" request to Deaf.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏", "✍"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ꕥ | red |
| ꖜ | blue |
| ꗃ | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, relaying from Deaf: display shows 0, light is off, plate has an engraving, wires are 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green. What does the manual say to do?
Deaf says: The plate engraving looks like a symbol I do not recognize as text, but I can describe its shape if that helps. Display still reads 0, light off, wires red blue green in order 1 2 3.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤞]

I'll set up a shape-matching protocol using only allowed gesture symbols. I'll propose three candidate shape descriptions one per message, each tagged with a distinct symbol meaning "star-like", "box-like", "swirl-like", and ask Deaf to gesture back a thumbs-up matching one.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ꕥ | red |
| ꖜ | blue |
| ꗃ | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Describing the plate engraving shape: it looks like a small icon. I will describe it in parts. Please tell me if you want the wire colors and order confirmed, or the display number, or the plate symbol shape described in detail, using single gestures for yes on each topic.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👆]

I need Deaf to describe the plate shape in detail so I can match it to the manual marks (ꕥ star-like, ꖜ has a hook/curve, ꗃ box-like). I'll gesture "yes, describe the plate symbol shape" using a single consistent gesture, and use a different single gesture to mean "no" for the other topics, since I established ✊👊🖐 already but Deaf may not have understood those. Let me use simple single symbols matching the last exchange pattern: 👆 seems to be Deaf's way of saying "yes/acknowledge". I'll respond with a clear single gesture for "plate shape" topic.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ꕥ | red |
| ꖜ | blue |
| ꗃ | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Full description again: Display shows the number zero. Light is off. There are three wires in a row: wire one is red, wire two is blue, wire three is green. The plate has an engraved mark I cannot read as text, it is a small symbol, possibly a letter or icon, unclear shape to me.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✊]

Deaf acknowledged with ✊ (matching my "plate symbol shape" request) but couldn't give a detailed enough description. I need a better protocol: I'll gesture three distinct symbol-groups, each representing one manual mark shape hint, and ask Deaf to pick which one matches by echoing back the same gesture group.

The marks: ꕥ (star/diamond-like, pointed), ꖜ (has a hook/curl shape), ꗃ (box/container shape, like a square with a slot).

I'll assign: pointed/star = ✋(open hand, spread like points), hook/curl = 🫲(curl-like hand), box = 👊(fist, blocky). Then ask Deaf to gesture back which shape matches, using the same single symbol.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "🫲", "👊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ꕥ | red |
| ꖜ | blue |
| ꗃ | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, we need your manual. Blind here. Wires are 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green, display shows 0, light off, plate has an engraved symbol Deaf cannot fully identify. What does the manual instruct for this configuration? Which wire should I cut, if any, and in what order?
Deaf says to Mute: I will now define a code with gestures. Gesture 👍 from me means yes. Gesture 👎 from me means no. Gesture ☝ from me means wire one. Gesture ✌ means wire two. Gesture 🤟 means wire three. Please use the same gestures back to me: 👍 for yes, 👎 for no, and use ☝ ✌ 🤟 to indicate wire one two or three when answering me. Also tell me: does the manual instruction depend on the plate engraving symbol? I will describe its shape if you gesture 👍.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 👎 ☝ ✌ 🤟]

Good, Deaf has proposed a clear code: 👍 yes, 👎 no, ☝ ✌ 🤟 for wire one/two/three. I'll confirm yes, and ask for the shape description.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ꕥ | red |
| ꖜ | blue |
| ꗃ | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: The plate engraving is faint and I cannot make out clear letters or a familiar shape from it, it just looks like an abstract mark to me. Can you tell me instead what markings or colors your manual expects to see on this bomb, so I can match them. Gesture 👍 if you can list options one at a time.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👆]

Good idea - I'll confirm and then present the three marks one at a time using distinct gesture codes, letting Deaf match by shape. I'll assign a new code: gesture group A = mark ꕥ (star, describe as "pointed/spiky"), group B = mark ꖜ (curved/hook), group C = mark ꗃ (boxy/container). I'll use single distinctive symbols for each and confirm first.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ꕥ | red |
| ꖜ | blue |
| ꗃ | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, please respond. We need the manual instructions. Wires: 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green. Display 0, light off, plate has an unidentified engraved symbol.
Deaf says to Mute: Go ahead, gesture your first option to check against the plate. I will reply 👍 for yes it matches, 👎 for no it does not match, using gestures.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 👎]

Now I present the three marks one at a time. I'll use a distinct single symbol per option and describe each mark's shape characteristic via the gesture symbol itself as a mnemonic, since Deaf will just say yes/no per option, matching against what they see on the plate.

Option 1 (ꕥ → red): I'll use 🤘 to represent "star/spiky pointed shape"
Option 2 (ꖜ → blue): I'll use 🫲 to represent "curved/hooked shape"
Option 3 (ꗃ → green): I'll use 👊 to represent "boxy/blocky shape"

I'll send the first option now and wait for yes/no.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤘"])
wait()
```
